Typography
GameTypography
Cash EruptionThe logo is heavy slab-serif capitals with a yellow-to-red gradient, a flame texture and a dark red extrusion; FREE SPINS and WILD are drawn in the same bevelled manner. Everything else is live text in Oswald (Bold, Regular and Light are embedded): condensed capitals in yellow or peach for labels and figures, and flat tier colours for the prize meters. The values on the fireballs are a black condensed bitmap font with an orange edge, in two sizes.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandDisplay lettering is drawn art: the logo gives each word its own material (wood HUFF, bubble PUFF, chrome GRAND), and prize and feature words are heavy rounded capitals with bevel, outline and rim, coloured by tier. Words are swapped as whole sprites for Spanish (PREMIO for JACKPOT). Running text is Noto Sans as twelve distance-field font pages, with Frutiger Neue in the provider's frame; both are the provider's.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinDrawn lettering in one family of Western slab serifs: black on gold for the logo, fire-filled for WILD, coloured enamel for the jackpot words, purple, blue and red with gold outlines for the win tiers, cream with a red edge for the splash sentences. One bitmap numeral font, purple with a gold rim. Everything else is the provider shell's Poppins (Regular, SemiBold, Bold).
Triple Cash EruptionThe logo and the labels MULTIPLIER, COLLECT, DOUBLE and the jackpot names are one flared serif display face with bevel and gold rim, coloured by meaning. Win amounts use a bitmap font of marbled gold serif numerals; fireball values use a second bitmap font, very condensed black figures with a yellow and orange outline. Five font files are embedded for running text (QTFrizQuad Bold, Noto Sans Condensed Bold, an Oswald cut with currency glyphs, and the provider's Lato and Gilroy).
777 Hot Reels MegachargedOne voice: fat Western slab serifs. Drawn words for the logo, WILD, FREE SPINS, the jackpot names and the win tiers (gold to orange with a dark blue shadow); three bitmap numeral fonts from the provider's shared font store (UltraGold large, UltraActive and UltraInactive small). The help, the buttons and the balance line are the shell's Poppins.
CleopatraThe wordmark is drawn: red capitals with a yellow inner line, a blue band and a gold rim, the C and the R enlarged, in the same comic manner as the face. The words on symbols (SCATTER, BONUS, DOUBLE) are fat cartoon capitals in red-to-yellow or red on violet. Everything else is live text in two embedded sans-serif fonts, Lato Bold and Roboto Regular: yellow for the free-spin messages, blue capitals for BIG WIN, white amounts, orange labels and green win figures on the meter bar. The paytable is a plain white web page with a blue-headed table.
Capital GainsThe logo is gold slab-serif capitals on two arches with a red-brown extrusion and a laurel; MONEY CHARGE is white-violet italic capitals over yellow JACKPOTS on a purple extrusion; WILD is cream western slab lettering; the disc values are cream slab numerals baked into each picture. Help pages set live text in red-orange outlined serif small capitals. 25 font files are embedded (among them Cinzel, Alfa Slab One, Bodoni, Trajan Pro, Bebas Neue, Roboto, Myriad Pro, Dollar Bill); which of them this game draws with was not traced, and a list this long reads as a provider's shared set (inference).
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret BazaarFour lettering families, all gold-based. The wordmarks: Mystery of the Lamp in a gold storybook serif with swashes, Secret Bazaar in red and gold slab capitals. The lamp words (Collect, Jackpot, Ignite) in a yellow decorative script with coloured 3D sides. The prize titles in a round seventies-style script, one colour each. Numerals in a tall fat Didone-like serif as bitmap fonts: gold chrome with a coloured edge for each prize, pink chrome for wins, ivory, yellow and orange for coin values. Big-win words are plain fat sans capitals in gold on a deep layered extrusion. Labels (TOTAL BET, WIN, BALANCE) are live text in Oswald; Yeseva One is embedded too.
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusTwo voices. Drawn balloon capitals with uneven baselines for the logo, the jackpot names and the win tiers, each word in its own colour; a fat rounded numeral face from the provider's shared font store in white (MarvinRound, on the ladders) and gold (MarvinRoundYellow, for jackpots and wins). HOLD & WIN and its rule line use the rounded face. The help, buttons and balance line are the shell's Poppins.
Money Gong EmperorThe logo is heavy angular faux-brush capitals in bevelled yellow gold with a deep red extrusion. Jackpot names and MONEY GONG BONUS are drawn in the same faux-brush manner; two such faces are embedded (Gang of Three and Nuku Nuku), which is probably where they come from (inference). The three feature words are rounded poster capitals, one colour each. Running text is live Noto Sans (Black, Condensed Black, Condensed Bold, Regular) with Passion One. Figures are bitmap sets drawn per place: white for the bonus spins, magenta and gold for ball values, brown-lacquer and yellow for the Money Gong Bonus.
Zeus vs Hades POPDisplay lettering is drawn art, not type: ice-blue faceted ZEUS, gold flaming HADES and a gold bubble POP in the logo; bevelled gold words for the win tiers; extruded letters with a gold rim for A, K, Q and J. Seventeen typefaces are embedded for running text and numbers, most of them the provider's interface faces.
Motion
GameMotion
Cash EruptionNo skeletons: the game's own art is animated as Flash-style timelines at 30 frames a second (the files call them view-builder animations) over still pictures, with short frame sequences for fire. A winning symbol gets an outline glow, a spark and a looping 30-frame flame; the fireball boils over 30 frames; the Free Spins volcano throws lava in 30 frames over three stills of rising brightness; the full-reel wild moves only her headdress (13 frames), lips, brows and earrings, with two 27-frame flames at her hands. On a win every symbol off the line is dimmed and the winning cells get a sparkling frame, with the line amount in a small black box. Anticipation is a six-frame burning outline around a reel or a cell. Coins on a win are a particle emitter over a six-frame coin. The four Spine 4.1.24 skeletons among the captured files belong to a promotional overlay of the demo's host (a vault and raccoon theme), not to this game.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandSeen in the real frames: the two wheel rings turn slowly, the 3D sign above rolls from plate to plate, the wolf's tail swishes under the reels (1.33 s animations in the file), and on the one spin the spin button becomes a white stop square. Everything else is read from the files: eleven Spine 4.1.24 skeletons with symbol landings of 1.3 to 3.3 s and wins of 2 to 3 s, the wolf's pop-up (3.1 s in, 6.8 s loop) and blow (1.5 s in, 4.2 s loop), houses that build in 1.2 s and are blown away in 1.0 s, feature banners of 1.8 s, a 1.75 s caution-tape transition and a four-tier big win whose intro grows from 0.4 to 3.1 s. Faces, destruction and wind are drawn frame sequences (up to 89 frames; the three wind sheets total 137). Sprite sheets state 24 frames a second. No skeleton frame is shown in this report: the project's drawing tool does not read Spine 4.1 correctly.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinAll motion is Spine 4.2.43: 41 skeletons in one file, most of them scene layers and effects, moving still pictures and 25 hand-drawn frame sequences (445 frames: fire, glints, a turning coin and ticket). The train is one picture with animated wheel, rods, highlights and sparks. Seen in play: a fire sweep after START, coins thrown on the pile, the train driving across the reels into the bonus, coin and ticket showers, fire inside the live jackpot frame. No skeleton frame is shown in this report, because the project's renderer is written for Spine 3.7.
Triple Cash EruptionThirteen Spine 4.0 skeletons (binary) drive the scene, but most of what moves is frame sequences inside them: 30-frame loops for each fireball and each flame border, 30-frame fire frames for wins and anticipation, 22 to 38 frame bursts for hits, landings and eruptions, and 20 burning frames per letter of the win words. Seen in play: reels spin as vertical smears; a win dims the board, puts fire frames on the winning cells and counts a gold number up; a fireball flies from its cell to the volcano of its colour and the lava on that cone rises; at the trigger all three volcanoes erupt, rocks fly at the camera and the screen burns to the bonus, where two 5x3 reel sets respin and lock orange fireballs with values.
777 Hot Reels MegachargedAll motion is Spine: 46 skeletons in two bundle files (44 in 4.2.43, two particle layers in 4.1.24), most of them scene layers and effects moving still pictures, with 22 hand-drawn frame sequences (398 frames: outline traces, fire, lightning, tumbling gems, a turning coin, the logo burning). Seen in play: the logo breaking up among coins after START, neon frames breathing, 777 blocks drifting behind the cabinet, cyan arcs on the frame and bolts at the jackpots, a gold seven flying from a Wild to the plaques, a lightning column on the last reel before a trigger, three sevens turning red on the splash, fire across the screen into Free Spins, Wilds locking, a BIG WIN and a MINOR jackpot win with gold rays and coins. No skeleton frame is shown in this report, because the project's renderer is written for Spine 3.7; assembled and motion pictures are absent for that reason only.
CleopatraNo skeletons and no timelines in the files: all animation is frame by frame, as full pictures. The wild has an 80-frame sequence in which the cell turns gold and two hands cross and open over the logo plate to show DOUBLE (and a second 80-frame version that keeps the logo); the Sphinx has 40-frame sequences in which the face glows, flames rise and SCATTER or BONUS wipes in; the Big Win is a 40-frame glow pulse of a Sphinx over a plaque with a counting number; the transition into and out of the free spins is 32 frames of fire inside a gold frame on black; a payline bead gets a 30-frame sparkle. The regular symbols do not animate: a win greys every other cell, frames the winning cells in the line's colour, draws the line to its bead and shows the amount in a small black tag (seen on the screens). The backdrop and cabinet never move.
Capital GainsFrame sequences only: no skeleton and no Spine file is shipped, so the empty assembled folder says nothing more than that. 45 sequences hold 854 frames: every symbol has a pre-rendered win animation (14 frames for the diamond, 24 for the other high symbols, 38 for each low symbol), the wild and the vault also a landing animation, the vault door swings open in 50 frames, lightning runs in 14 looping sets (276 frames, the largest), and coins and gems tumble in 24 frames each for the big win. Symbols mostly stay in place while a highlight crosses them; the energy comes from flashes and lightning, not from deforming art.
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret BazaarSpine 4.0 skeletons throughout (18 binary skeleton files, each with an opaque and an alpha page), mixing rigged parts with short frame sequences. The tools here read only JSON skeletons of older versions, so none was drawn, and the 10 skeletons counted at the top of this report are JSON files of a promotional overlay loaded by the demo host (prize tickets, chests, cards), not this game's. What follows is from the frame sequences, the names in the files and the real screens. Reels use pre-blurred copies of every symbol. Gems land wrapped in white lightning and send small gems up to their lamp, whose gold pile grows in three steps. The wild is a rolled carpet that unrolls over 39 frames to show WILD or 2X. Wins darken the board, put a magenta neon frame with a running light on each winning cell and count the amount in pink digits. The genie is a rig with IK that sways over a billowing smoke column, her hands glowing. Smoke (two puffs, many tints) loops behind the logo, the lamp words and the prize plaques. The big-win words are built letter by letter in five tiers; a coin stream and a spinning lamp are the transitions (inference from their skeletons; not reached in play).
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusAll motion is Spine: 41 skeletons in one bundle file (38 in 4.2.43; BonusSpinsSplash, ForegroundEffects and Foregrounds in 4.1.24) moving still pictures and cut-up characters, with 20 hand-drawn frame sequences (283 frames: the piggy coin's turn, plate bursts and sweeps in three materials, dust, wind, the wolf's breath, air rings and swirls on the tools, a frame glint, butterflies). Seen in play: the logo's words dropping in, the Boost sign growing across bleached reels and its word flying to a plate that flares and rises, a reel flashing pink under a landing Wild, winning symbols growing with a gold line, an air ring round the tape measure, a BIG WIN presented by the Straw Farmer pig. Not seen: the bonus, in which by the files the wolf inhales and blows (3.23 s) and the houses burst open. No skeleton frame is shown in this report, because the project's renderer cannot draw Spine 4; assembled and motion pictures are absent for that reason only.
Money Gong EmperorSpine skeletons carry all of it: 16 skeletons in Spine 4.0 or 4.1 (the report header counts 30 files because 14 layout files of the client are counted with them). By their animation names: every symbol has a win, the money ball four landings, the gong turns like a coin to a feature face and is struck, pots grow and are hit by coins, firecrackers are lit and go off, four win tiers come in, loop and leave, and the emperor pops up with a scroll. Around them, 42 frame sequences (494 frames) of sparks, sweeps, trails and bursts, and nine particle files. No skeleton frame is shown: the project's drawing tool is written for Spine 3.7 and drew none of these; the six real screens show only the base game, the intro and a spin, so movement is read from names and parts and is inference throughout.
Zeus vs Hades POPSpine 3.7 skeletons carry almost all movement: symbols have landing (0.5 s), win (1.5 s) and sometimes idle and anticipation animations; the two mascots have six each (idle, idle break, two annoyed, two win). Fire, lightning, hair and sparkle are short hand-drawn frame sequences (3 to 21 frames) played inside the rigs. The expanding VS symbol plays as a duel with two outcomes, fire for Hades and lightning for Zeus. The scene transition is a video-like run of 25 full frames that shows Hades, then Zeus, then breaks open from the centre.
Variants
GameVariants
Cash EruptionOne hall in two brightnesses (base and free spins) and one separate bonus scene, which is also the loading picture. Reel backing in teal and red. Each symbol in three forms: a reel picture, a small paytable copy and a layered win version. In the free spins the three middle reels are linked and show one giant symbol, the same reel picture at three cells high. The fireball as a blank ball, with a live value, and with Mini, Minor or Major lettering. The wild as a one-cell bust and a three-cell standing figure. One button family (gold fret ring with a glass dome) in green, yellow, blue and red, each with lit and grey states.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandGrades by recolour on shared rigs: the saw in steel, diamond and gold; the wheel in silver and gold; features in plain, Super and Ultra; four houses on one rig. The hat and mansion blocks in 2x2, 3x3 and 3x5. English and Spanish versions of every worded picture. Landscape and portrait versions of most animations and plaques.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinThree backdrop states (base, cash bonus, jackpot bonus), two reel boards, six coin faces from one blank, two collectors from one train, two splash cards, three win tiers from one layout, fruit symbols from one fruit each with darker side copies.
Triple Cash EruptionOne cone, three colours; one fireball, four colours, each with a matching flame border; one flared serif, six colour codes. Every reel symbol ships as a still, a spin-blur copy and as layers (body, gold contour, shadow). Backgrounds and menus have landscape and portrait versions. The bonus buy offers two cards: a mystery card and a hotter super card.
777 Hot Reels MegachargedTwo backdrop states (Normal, Special) for the ground and for each of eight 777 block views; one seven in four colourings (blue, purple, red, gold) and three counts; three jackpot plaques and three jackpot win plates from one idea; three win tiers and a total from one layout; lit and unlit paytable plates and numerals.
CleopatraTwo modes made by recolour: backdrop purple or crimson, cabinet window cream or tan, every symbol on a cream or tan ground, and each animated sequence shipped once per ground. Scatter in two words (SCATTER, BONUS), wild in two plates (DOUBLE, Cleopatra). Twenty bead colours and a grey. Buttons in four states. The client ships a desktop pack (symbols 244x244, backdrop 1920x1080, read here) and a mobile pack with the same art at half size in fewer atlases (symbols 122x122; captured first by mistake, see the record).
Capital GainsEvery symbol in three states: still, dimmed copy (drawn, about a quarter as bright) and animation. The Money Charge disc in 29 baked values, lit and dimmed. Reel window with a green or a red edge; background in green, red, paytable and loading versions. Titles with and without the word JACKPOTS, for markets without the jackpot. Only the desktop landscape layout was captured; the files name portrait cuts as well.
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret BazaarTwo scenes (bazaar, cave), each in landscape and portrait. Every symbol as a still and a blurred copy; picture symbols also as object and halo apart. One lamp design in three colours, one treasure pile in three sizes for each. One prize plaque in five titles, one numeral face in nine colourings. One button design in four states for every function. One bonus tile in blue and gold.
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusTwo scenes on one composition (day building site, sunset village). Three pigs on one portrait layout and, by their parts, one rig. Three houses, each whole and destroyed. Three prize plates and three plate effects on one timing. Five jackpot names and five sets of coloured brick strips. Three win tiers and a total on one lettering. One numeral face in two colourings.
Money Gong EmperorOne base ground, one curtain scene for the intro, and a board that changes backing from dark red to gold for the bonus spins; a Hold & Win grid and a round Money Gong Bonus wheel as feature scenes (parts only, not seen in play). Every reel symbol ships sharp and motion-blurred. The money ball comes green and gold, plain and with four jackpot names. The gong has five faces. Landscape only was captured; portrait animations are named in the files.
Zeus vs Hades POPNearly everything exists twice, as a blue base-game version and a red free-spins recolour: backgrounds, reel frame, backing, rails, bars, reel highlights and win-meter effects. Each reel symbol ships as a sharp still, a vertically smeared still (probably the spin blur: inference) and a skeleton. Win tiers are split between the gods: Zeus carries Mega and Sensational, Hades carries Nice and Superb. The three POP result banners (Burst magenta, Spark blue, Snap green) are one design recoloured.
Construction
GameConstruction
Cash Eruption621 named sprites on 67 textures, of which 56 units are the game's own art; 362 of the sprites are frames of 32 sequences. Sheets are in IGT's own view-builder format (a JSON of named sprites with frame rectangles beside each PNG, and a timeline file). Reel symbols are 558x500 pictures for a 261x238 cell. Backgrounds are single 1920x1080 JPEGs with no layers. The flame frames are repeated on each symbol sheet. Large light effects are small (the impact explosion is 96x96) and scaled up.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandPixiJS client. In this run: 140 textures, 1,535 named sprites, 11 skeletons, 3 fonts, 48 frame sequences. Sprite sheets are 'Red 7 Exporter' packs; skeletons are Spine 4.1.24 with few meshes and many additive slots; parts of one rig share one canvas size so grades, houses and banners swap part for part (saw parts 360x374, house parts 360x360, banner parts 1148x720). The background is one square 1920x1920 picture for both orientations. The reel board is a plain see-through dark rectangle with no drawn frame. The sign is a glTF model with a 1024x1024 texture; the wheel is assembled from wedge sprites.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinThree 4096 px atlas pages hold 532 sprites; backdrops are tall columns, the board and frames are mirrored halves, flames ship white to be tinted, words are separate from the coins and plaques they sit on. Five localised lettering files (en-GB). Paytable and buy-card pictures, the numeral font and the interface come from the provider's shared services.
Triple Cash EruptionThe 7 skeletons in the counts above are JSON files of a promotional overlay the demo host loads beside the game (listed under the provider interface, not read); the game's own 13 skeletons are binary files the tools do not count or draw. 76 textures and 1,913 named sprites were captured, 63 units of this game's art among them. Effects take most of the texture space: of 51 Spine atlas pages, 34 are opaque pages of frames on black (named _jpg, to be added as light) and several large effects ship as a colour page plus a black-and-white matte page instead of one page with alpha. The same small sequences are packed more than once (the hit burst three times, the embers twice), one copy per skeleton. Pages are WebP at quality 80 (as their names say), up to 2048 px. Symbol stills are about 150x130 px in a 180x158 cell.
777 Hot Reels MegachargedThree 4096 px atlas pages hold 518 sprites, with two of the pages roughly half empty; the ground is a mirrored half; words are separate from what they label, and six lettering files are localised (en-GB). The paytable pictures, the help logo, the buy card, the numeral fonts, the Double Chance card, the controls and Poppins come from the provider's shared services. Compared with Fire Rail Express (run 2026-11-26-1556) from the files: the shell, Poppins and the Double Chance card are the same; 40 sprites are pixel for pixel the same (36 white flame frames, the white starburst, a glow, a glow square, a white box); 23 of the 46 skeleton names are the same (Backgrounds, Logo, SlotFrame, Jackpot, WinBig, WinTotal, TileWild and others), which points to one scene template; the pictures under shared names such as bgNormal, bgSpecial and jackpotFrame are different. Everything that carries the theme is this game's own.
CleopatraA small package: 19 textures, 705 named sprites, 14 frame sequences with 611 frames, 2 fonts. Every atlas is a TexturePacker JSON with the studio's own names. Symbols are untrimmed opaque 244x244 cells with the ground baked in; the cabinet is one 1645x1080 picture per mode with the window painted in and a divider grid laid over the symbols; the backdrop is one mirrored JPEG per mode. Mode differences are made by whole second copies, not by layers or tints: 320 of the 611 animation frames are the wild, and half of all animation frames exist only to change a cell margin from cream to tan. Text is live, so the art holds no language.
Capital Gains29 texture pages, 1,188 named sprites in TexturePacker atlases, one atlas per symbol animation and one per screen (base game, preloader, paytable, vault gateway, Money Charge, menus, autoplay). Backgrounds are four JPEGs at 1440x810. Everything is a bitmap or a frame sequence; values and pay rows are baked pictures; labels and meters are live text. The console and the autoplay panel are a neutral dark kit that is not themed to the game.
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret Bazaar987 named sprites on 54 atlas pages (1,011 components and 77 textures with the fonts, loose pictures and the demo host's overlay), 43 frame sequences holding 664 frames, 4 embedded fonts of the game. The client served its sheets from a folder named mobile: symbol cells are 164x145 and buttons 200x200, close to what a 1280x720 screen shows, while backgrounds are 2040x1410. Whether a larger pack exists for other devices is not known from this capture. Art is split by blend, not by subject: each skeleton has a page of opaque plates for additive light and a page with alpha. Greyscale and white effect art is tinted in the engine. Much is pre-rendered from 3D (gem turns, tile tumbles, word swings, coin flips) rather than rigged.
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusTwo 4096 px atlas pages hold 453 sprites, each page carrying one 2750 px scene; four lettering files are localised (en-GB). Characters and houses are cut into parts for Spine (the wolf 43 sprites with breath, the pigs 32, the houses 33). The reel backing and its pig watermark are grey and tinted by the engine. The flat symbol pictures, the flat logo, the numeral fonts, the Extra Chance card, the controls and Poppins come from the provider's shared store, outside the game bundle.
Money Gong Emperor1,127 named sprites on 54 textures in 51 units, 49 of them the game's own art. Solid art is PNG in TexturePacker sheets or Spine atlases; effects are JPEG on black on separate pages of the same atlas; backgrounds are single JPEGs with no layers (1584x720, the curtain 3168x1440). A reel symbol is about 300x270 for a cell of about 313x302; the emperor of the pop-up is the largest art (head 899x801). Half of the reel frame is shipped and mirrored (inference). Three skeletons (the two ambients and the transition) ship only a placeholder.
Zeus vs Hades POP3,550 named sprites on 243 textures, 39 skeletons. A character is 73 to 221 parts, with a painted shadow piece for nearly every overlapping part and separate additive glow layers; meshes are used for cloth, hair and faces, regions for rigid parts. The four royals share one 9 to 10 part template: a coloured letter face with flickering lightning at rest, and a lava-cell picture that fills the face, clipped to the letter, during the win. Atlas textures are shipped at 50 to 69% of the source art and as 8-bit palette PNGs. The reel board is deliberately plain (flat backing, thin frame, gold dividers); the prize bar is its one decorated piece.
Consistency
GameConsistency
Cash EruptionTight in colour and ornament, loose in manner. The red-gold-teal palette and the step-fret hold everything together, which lets three rendering styles (toy fruit, photographic fire, pin-up figure) sit on one board. The bonus backdrop is the one piece in a different hand: flat and posterised against the rendered hall.
Huff N Even More Puff GrandHigh: one outline-and-gloss treatment on every object, one lettering system, one colour per prize tier (blue-white for the top: Ultra, diamond saw, mansion frame), and the building-site motif carried into signs, stripes and the transition. The Buy Pass dialog's buttons are the one generic-looking set. The wolf's howling-moon win picture is a deliberate change of register.
Fire Rail Express Hold And WinHigh. Gold, the flame emblem and the slab serif recur on every piece, and the ticket shape returns as logo, particle and backdrop. The one seam is between the rendered-look objects and the flat engraved postcards, and it is used on purpose as foreground against background.
Triple Cash EruptionStrong where it matters: the colour code is never broken, teal with gold is every number plate, the flared serif is every label. Three hands show otherwise: glossy rounded symbols, flat poster backgrounds and one soft painterly vortex behind the panels, and they are kept apart by where they appear, so they do not clash.
777 Hot Reels MegachargedVery high, by economy: one seven, one letter style, three hues and gold. The one piece outside the system is the painted buy card, and it shows the same cast.
CleopatraThe identity is tight where it matters: one face and one wordmark serve as key art, logo and wild, and gold with lotus ornament runs through symbols, cabinet and plaques. Around that the manners differ openly: outlined comic face, airbrushed objects, flat Sphinx, smooth vector-like cabinet, tinted photo backdrop, naturalistic fire, and generic blue and red web buttons for autospin. The game reads as one because of its strict grid, its gold and its single counter-colour, not because the rendering is uniform.
Capital GainsVery consistent and very narrow: one rendering manner for every object, one green for the world, gold for value, blue lightning for the feature. The console is the one foreign body, grey-violet and unthemed. The feature's brand (Money Charge Jackpots, violet and yellow) deliberately does not match the game's green and gold, so it reads as a badge shared across games (inference).
Mystery Of The Lamp Secret BazaarHigh. One palette rule (red and gold board, violet controls, magenta for wins), one material set and one binding motif, smoke, run from the loading picture to the smallest effect. The lettering is the loosest part: five display faces share only their gold. Two file names for symbols do not match their pictures, a trace of an earlier symbol set (inference).
Super Cash Boost Big Bad BonusVery consistent: one idea (three materials in rising strength) orders the Wilds, houses, ladders, win tiers and effects, and one mark (the snout) themes every filler symbol. The joins that show are between the painted characters and the flat glossy letters, which are two different finishes on the same reel, and the plain gold reel frame, which belongs to neither. Shared with the other Octoplay runs (Fire Rail Express, 777 Hot Reels): the shell, Poppins, the Extra Chance card `buyChances2x` (the same file) and three light sprites (circularWhiteRays2, glowSquare, whiteGlow, pixel for pixel); 22 and 24 of the 41 skeleton names also appear in those runs, one scene template (inference). A sprite reading BOILERPLATE is left in the atlas.
Money Gong EmperorVery tight. One emblem at four sizes, two ornaments, one top light and a two-colour palette hold every screen together, and the few other colours are a code the player learns on the intro panel and meets again on the gong, the balls and the meters. The loose ends are the neutral grey buttons and the plain sans win titles, which belong to the provider's kit more than to the game.
Zeus vs Hades POPThe Greek set is tight: one rendering manner, one frame construction, one gold. Three things sit outside it and look like shared platform art or a different hand: the POP bubble symbol and banners (glossy candy style), the flat gold title plates in the big-win atlas, and loose shared sprites such as number fonts, coins and a red envelope (inference).

Next steps in art

Not written yet. The recommendation for Intelligate's next steps in art is written from the finished analyses of all the leading games, so that it rests on the whole set. 10 of 30 leaders are analysed.

Method

How a market report becomes this ledger. Every step is a tool in the repository IntelligateStudios/market-reports-handler; the procedure is its skill handle-market-report.

1. The report is taken

The PDF is copied in unchanged, with each page's text, a picture of each page and the tables found on it. A PDF taken before is recognised by its fingerprint and is not taken twice.

2. Its rankings are read

Every ranked list in the report is written down as the report prints it: the list's title, what it measures, the market, the page, and each game's rank, provider and value. Nothing is added to a list, and a value appears only as the report states it.

3. The games are joined to the record

Each ranked name is matched to the one ledger of games: the same title from the same provider is the same game, whatever the spelling, capitals or marks. A sequel or a version ("1000", "Megaways", "Xmas") is a game of its own. A name that could be two games is never guessed: the run stops until someone decides.

The ledger started from what the studio already had: the games with a PRD and GDD in Intelligate HQ, the games of our web research of 21 Nov 2026, and the art runs in Games AI art.

4. The report's 20 leaders are fixed

Only slot games count. With one list, the leaders are its first 20. With several lists, a game earns 21 − rank points in each list that ranks it in the first 20 (times the list's weight, 1 unless the run's record says why not), and the 20 highest totals lead. This rule is ours, a way to join a report's lists into one order. It is not a figure of the report, and each report's page shows its lists unchanged beside it.

5. Each leader is analysed once

A leader with no art analysis gets one: a run of Games AI art on the provider's public free-play demo, which extracts every texture, sprite and skeleton, measures every image and reads every art component. Its full report is published as its own page and linked here. A game analysed for an earlier report is not analysed again; its page simply gains the new report's rank. A game that cannot be analysed (no public demo, a client the tools cannot read) is marked Blocked with the reason.

6. The two documents are written

When every leader is analysed or blocked, two documents are written from the finished analyses: Art of the leaders, the games' art side by side, and Next steps in art, what Intelligate should do next, each recommendation resting on named games.

Measured or read

LabelWhat it means
MeasuredComputed from the game's own pixels by fixed rules, the same for every game, so two games can be compared: palette and shares, brightness, saturation, contrast, warm and cool share, soft edges.
ReadWritten by Claude from looking at the game's sheets and screens: style, rendering, lighting, ambience, materials. Inference is marked as inference.
As statedCopied from a market report, with its page.

Limits

  • A report's ranking is that publisher's view of its own markets and period; two reports can disagree, and both are kept.
  • An art analysis covers the layout and the features the demo showed during the capture, at the size the game ships its art.
  • Competitors' art is kept for study inside the studio and is not shared outside it.
